$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every capacity limit in this project (spec §79).
Imported by the web app, by the Cloud Functions, and checked against the
hardcoded literals in firestore.rules / storage.rules by a drift test.
Change a number here and nowhere else; the test will tell you what else
needs updating.
Allowances are the Blaze plan's no-cost tier as published at
https://firebase.google.com/pricing, read 2026-08-04. They are recorded
here so the derivation of every cap is auditable rather than folklore.
IMPORTANT: this project's bucket is labresults-2a13f.firebasestorage.app,
a *.firebasestorage.app bucket. Its allowances differ substantially from
the legacy *.appspot.com ones — notably upload operations, which are
5K PER MONTH here versus 20K per DAY on a legacy bucket. Do not copy
limits from appspot documentation.
Every app cap is 80% of the no-cost allowance unless stated otherwise.
The 20% headroom absorbs the counter drift described in `enforcement`
below, and means crossing a cap costs nothing — it is a warning line,
not a cliff. Storage is set tighter still (see storage.globalBytes).
globalBytes is 4 GiB against a 5 GB allowance — deliberately below the
0.8 policy margin, because the allowance may be quoted in decimal GB
(5.0e9 bytes) rather than binary GiB (5.37e9). 4 GiB = 4.295e9 bytes is
under either reading, so the cap holds whichever unit Google means.
UPLOAD OPERATIONS ARE THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, NOT STORAGE. At 4000
uploads/month across the planned ceiling of 10 users, that is 400
uploads per user per month — while 400 MiB of storage holds roughly 200
typical 2 MiB reports in total. A user hits the monthly op budget long
before they fill their space. Note also that a resumable upload can
consume more than one operation, so treat 4000 as optimistic.
AI spend is NOT a Firebase allowance and is not covered by the Blaze
caps above — it is billed separately by Google's Gemini API. These are
app-level budgets, chosen to keep usage inside the Gemini free tier and
to bound the damage if something loops.
PRIVACY: on the Gemini FREE tier, Google's terms allow submitted content
to be used to improve their products. For laboratory reports that is a
disclosure obligation, not a footnote. Two mitigations are in place:
identifiers are redacted before every call (functions/src/ai/redaction.ts),
and the app reports the training status truthfully in AI metadata.
Setting GEMINI_BILLING_ENABLED=true after enabling billing moves the
project to the paid tier, where content is not used for training.
Cost, once billed: $0.30 per 1M input tokens, $2.50 per 1M output.
At ~4K tokens per report that is roughly $0.01 per report analysed.
$derivation: callsPerProjectPerDay is callsPerUserPerDay x the plannedUserCeiling of
10, so the project budget and the per-user budget cannot disagree.
50 calls/user/day is generous against real use — a report holds ~24
results and variable explanations are cached per variable, not per user.

$comment: Not a practical constraint: the storage caps put the planned ceiling at
10 concurrent users. Recorded for completeness and because a future
storage-tier change would make it relevant.
What is actually enforced, and how hard. Written down because a limit
nobody enforces is a wish, and a limit enforced only in the browser is
a suggestion.
HARD (denied server-side, cannot be bypassed):
- per-file size            storage.rules, on every create
- per-user stored bytes    storage.rules via firestore.get(usage/{uid})
- global stored bytes      storage.rules via firestore.get(systemUsage/global)
- per-user monthly uploads storage.rules via the same usage document
- the uploadsDisabled kill switch
SOFT (surfaced, not blocked): Firestore read/write/delete counts,
Functions invocations, egress. Counting these in-band would cost a
write per operation, which spends the very budget it protects. They
are covered by the GCP billing budget and alerting described in
docs/quotas.md instead.
KNOWN GAP — counter drift. The storage counters are updated by a
Storage-triggered function AFTER an object is finalized, so several
uploads racing in parallel can each pass the rule check before any
counter moves. Worst case overshoot is roughly
(concurrent uploads x maxFileBytes). Three things contain it: the client
uploads strictly one file at a time, the caps sit below the no-cost
allowance so an overshoot costs nothing, and reconcileUsage recomputes
true usage from the bucket every day and corrects the counters.

$ceilingComment: floor(globalBytes / perUserBytes) = 10. This is the number of users who
can hold a full quota at once, and it is what the per-user share of every
other budget is derived from. It is NOT enforced at registration —
real users rarely fill their quota, and locking out an 11th signup would
be a product decision, not an infrastructure one. The admin dashboard
warns when active users exceed it.
